lessons.title: How Balances Are Stored and Summarized

slots.practicalActivity: Tour the pre-configured Solara Fixtures, Inc. primary ledger in your practice environment end to end: open the General Ledger work area, confirm all four of the ledger's required components (chart of accounts, calendar, currency, accounting method -- the "four Cs"), and check the current status (Open, Future Enterable, or Closed) of each accounting period in the calendar.
slots.deliverable: A one-page setup-review note listing Solara Fixtures' four ledger components and the status of every accounting period you found in its calendar.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Journals work area, create a manual journal for Solara Fixtures recording a $1,250 March office supplies accrual (debit Office Supplies Expense, credit Accrued Liabilities), filling in all six header fields: Ledger, Journal Name, Accounting Date, Source (Manual), Category (Accrual), and Currency.
slots.deliverable: One saved manual journal with a complete header and two balanced lines, matching the accrual pattern worked in the lesson.

slots.practicalActivity: Build a journal batch with at least 3 lines spread across two different balancing segment (Company) values. Deliberately leave the batch unbalanced for one Company value, try to mark it Complete, read the resulting validation error, and then fix the line so both Company values net to zero before completing it again.
slots.deliverable: A journal batch that failed completion once with a documented validation error, then a corrected, successfully completed version of the same batch.

slots.practicalActivity: Post the corrected journal batch from the previous slot, confirming it updates the ledger's account balances. Then generate a reversing journal for it (for example because the accrual needs to be reversed in the following period), and post the reversal, confirming the original balances return to their pre-accrual state.
slots.deliverable: One posted original journal plus its posted reversing journal, with a before/after note on the affected account balances.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: without new instruction, enter and fully process three more varied manual journals for Solara Fixtures end to end -- a standard expense entry, a correcting entry for a miscoded account, and a second accrual -- practicing Save versus Complete at every step, and posting each one once it validates.
slots.deliverable: Three independently entered, validated, and posted journal batches, each demonstrating a different real-world journal scenario.

slots.practicalActivity: Submit a manual journal so it routes into the approval workflow rather than posting directly, and trace what happens to its status while pending approval. Separately, download the JournalImportTemplate.xlsm, populate the GL_INTERFACE worksheet with 5 rows of journal line data (ledger, date, currency, segments, debit/credit), and generate the CSV/zip the import process expects.
slots.deliverable: One journal submitted into approval with its pending status documented, plus a populated FBDI GL_INTERFACE spreadsheet with 5 ready-to-import rows.

slots.practicalActivity: Upload your FBDI file from the previous slot and run Import Journals, deliberately including one row with an invalid account combination so you can see and diagnose a real import-level rejection. Then define an Auto Post criteria set that automatically posts future Spreadsheet-source journals meeting specific category and ledger conditions.
slots.deliverable: One import run with a documented rejected row and its fix, plus one configured Auto Post criteria set.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable a suspense account on the Solara Fixtures ledger, then import or enter a journal that is deliberately out of balance for one balancing segment value, and confirm the system automatically books the difference to the suspense account rather than rejecting the entry outright. Review the resulting suspense account balance.
slots.deliverable: One journal that posted out of balance into the suspense account, with the resulting suspense balance documented and explained.

lessons.title: Recurring Journals: Skeleton, Standard and Formula

slots.practicalActivity: Define a Formula recurring journal for a fixed monthly rent allocation (same two accounts, same amount, every period), then generate it for the current open period and confirm it created a ready-to-review journal batch without re-typing the amounts.
slots.deliverable: One defined Formula recurring journal and one successfully generated journal batch produced from it.

slots.practicalActivity: Rebuild the lesson's facilities-cost worked example as a real mass allocation: define a $60,000 cost pool and allocate it across Manufacturing (80 headcount), Sales (30 headcount), and Admin (10 headcount) cost centers using the pool x (usage / total usage) formula, then run the allocation and confirm it generates one credit line relieving the pool and three debit lines matching your hand-calculated $40,000 / $15,000 / $5,000 split.
slots.deliverable: One run mass allocation producing a 4-line journal (1 credit, 3 debits) whose amounts match an independently hand-calculated allocation.

slots.practicalActivity: Copy one of your already-posted journals from Chapter 2 into a new accounting period, adjust at least one line amount to reflect a realistic change, and save it as a new draft journal ready for review rather than re-keying it from scratch.
slots.deliverable: One new-period journal created by copying and modifying an existing posted journal.

slots.practicalActivity: Run Inquire on Detail Balances for the Travel & Entertainment expense account for the current period, confirming the actual period-to-date figure. Then set up an Account Monitor watchlist containing that account plus 2-3 others you've posted activity to this course, so you can track their balances at a glance going forward.
slots.deliverable: One detail balance inquiry result for Travel & Entertainment, plus a configured Account Monitor watchlist of 3-4 accounts.

slots.practicalActivity: Open Account Inspector on the Travel & Entertainment account and pivot the balance by cost center to see whether activity is spread evenly or concentrated in one department. Then run a Trial Balance report for the current period and confirm total debits equal total credits across the whole ledger.
slots.deliverable: One Account Inspector pivot-by-cost-center view with a one-sentence finding, plus one balanced Trial Balance report.

slots.practicalActivity: Run an Account Analysis Report for the cost center you pivoted in the previous slot to see every journal line behind its balance, then pick one line that traces back to a subledger source (for example an imported Spreadsheet-source journal) and drill down to its originating transaction detail.
slots.deliverable: One Account Analysis Report with every contributing journal line, plus a documented drill-down from one of those lines to its source transaction.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter lab: given the scenario "March's Travel & Entertainment expense looks too high," without being told the cause in advance, triage it using only this chapter's tools in order -- Inquire on Detail Balances first to confirm the figure, Account Inspector pivoted by cost center to isolate where it concentrates, the Account Analysis Report for that cost center to review every line, and a subledger drill-down on any line that traces to one -- and reach a documented conclusion about whether the overage is legitimate.
slots.deliverable: A short written triage memo walking through all four tools in order and stating a final conclusion on the expense overage, backed by what each tool showed.

slots.practicalActivity: Enter a foreign currency journal for a GBP-denominated services invoice (8,500 GBP) against the USD ledger, selecting the Corporate rate type, and confirm Oracle Fusion automatically populates the accounted USD amount. Verify your entered-vs-accounted math matches the lesson's own worked conversion.
slots.deliverable: One entered GBP foreign currency journal with both its entered and accounted amounts documented and verified by hand.

slots.practicalActivity: Run period-end revaluation on the still-open GBP liability from the previous slot using an updated period-end rate, and confirm the resulting gain or loss is booked. Then run Translation on the same ledger to produce a reporting-currency (GBP) version of a USD trial balance, confirming it mirrors the same chart of accounts and calendar.
slots.deliverable: One revaluation run with its booked gain/loss documented, plus one translated trial balance in a second currency.

slots.practicalActivity: Enter an intercompany transaction between two legal entities (one owing the other for a shared service), confirming the Intercompany segment correctly identifies the counterparty entity on each side. Run the Intercompany Reconciliation Report and confirm the receivable and payable sides net to zero.
slots.deliverable: One balanced intercompany transaction pair plus a reconciliation report confirming the two sides net to zero.

slots.practicalActivity: Review the intercompany pair from the previous slot and confirm whether it is flagged for elimination in a consolidation, then write out, step by step, what would happen to the group's consolidated balances if that elimination flag were missing.
slots.deliverable: A short written explanation of the elimination flag's effect, including what the consolidated numbers would incorrectly show if it were missing.

slots.practicalActivity: Work through the period-end close checklist for the current period, and filter Manage Journals by status to find every Unposted and Error journal across all sources (manual, imported, recurring). Diagnose and resolve at least one error (an invalid account or closed-period reference) before moving on.
slots.deliverable: A completed close checklist up to the journal-review step, plus one documented error journal diagnosed and resolved.

slots.practicalActivity: With every journal cleared, change the current period's status to Closed in Manage Accounting Period and open the next period. If the next period is the first period of a new fiscal year, confirm that Retained Earnings absorbed the prior year's net income and that every income statement account reset to zero, rather than treating it as a manual step.
slots.deliverable: One period successfully closed and the next opened, plus (if applicable) a documented before/after showing the Retained Earnings sweep and income statement accounts resetting to zero.

slots.practicalActivity: Work through all three of the lesson's triage scenarios as a timed capstone exercise using only this course's own tools: (1) an expense that looks too high, triaged with Inquire on Detail Balances, Account Inspector, and the Account Analysis Report; (2) a period that won't close, triaged through Manage Journals and Manage Accounting Period; (3) US/UK intercompany balances that don't net to zero, triaged with the Intercompany Reconciliation Report, revaluation status, and consolidation elimination flags.
slots.deliverable: A completed triage runbook covering all three scenarios, documenting which tool resolved each one and the final conclusion reached.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After this course, a student can create, validate, post, and automate journals in Oracle Fusion General Ledger; run balance inquiries, allocations, and multi-currency transactions; and execute a full period and year-end close -- the core day-to-day skill set of a working General Ledger consultant.
